subject: Request: temporary deferment of pin for Vermilion-7B variant (tokenizer mismatch)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Park <sara@zenolabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary deferment of pin for Vermilion-7B variant (tokenizer mismatch)

Hi team —

Zeno Labs is planning to onboard Vermilion-7B (variant v1.3.0) to our hosted catalog next week as part of their Dedicated trial. Their QA ran a quick smoke and flagged a tokenizer/backwards-compatibility issue: outputs and embeddings are shifting for several canonical prompts (see attached sample_prompts_v2.csv and telemetry-diff-20270402.log).

Product asks: can we approve a temporary deferment of the automatic pin policy for the Vermilion v1.3.0 variant for 14 days while we validate tokenization alignment and run extended evals? The main customer ask is to not have a rolling pin applied immediately because Zeno’s regression thresholds will be tripped and they want time to test with their prompt set.

Engineering notes are needed on:
- whether the tokenizer change can be toggled at runtime or if it requires a model rebuild
- any KV cache/compat implications for active sessions
- whether we can serve an alternative tokenization shim for Zeno only (per-tenant override)

Operational asks: if we grant a deferment, what telemetry and guardrails should we require (canary percentage, blackout windows, automated rollback triggers)?

Irene/Markus/Aditya — can you weigh in on feasibility + estimated hours? Laura — can you confirm customer expectations and whether Zeno is flexible on a short freeze window versus a full pin?

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Program Manager, Model Intake
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Park <sara@zenolabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary deferment of pin for Vermilion-7B variant (tokenizer mismatch)

Thanks Dylan — quick context from the account side: Zeno is running a small pilot (2 reserved instances) and is within their trial period. They surfaced the difference when comparing embeddings used for similarity search in their search UX: recall dropped ~6% on their regression set. They prefer a short deferment rather than an immediate pin because they want to experiment with the new tokenizer but need time to confirm.

From a contract/SA perspective they asked for a 2-week window to validate; they are willing to accept a canary at 5% of traffic for the new variant if that helps. They are not asking for price concessions — just time to validate before a forced pin.

If we require them to run a side-by-side in their environment (we provide the model + shim), would that be acceptable to them? Sara, can you confirm?

Laura
Senior Product Manager — Customer Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Park <sara@zenolabs.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-03T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary deferment of pin for Vermilion-7B variant (tokenizer mismatch)

Laura — yes, 2 weeks would work. We can run a side-by-side with 5% canary. Our eng-ops team attached a short diff log in case it helps (sent to Dylan). If Redwood can provide a per-tenant tokenizer shim or let us pin to v1.2.7 within the trial, that would be ideal while we validate v1.3.0.

Happy to jump on a call if helpful.
Sara
Head of Platform — Zeno Labs
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary deferment of pin for Vermilion-7B variant (tokenizer mismatch)

Quick engineering readout:
- Tokenizer change in v1.3.0 is non-trivial: codepaths changed in the preprocessor and affect byte-level offsets. It is possible to provide two tokenizers in the runtime, but it requires a small serving-side shim (we can load an alternate tokenizer table at model load). That shim is ~1-2 engineer-days to implement and test (including unit tests for token-alignment).
- KV cache compatibility: sessions signed with the new tokenizer are incompatible with caches built under the old tokenizer — we must avoid cross-tenant cache reuse. We can enforce tenant-isolated KV namespaces to eliminate cross-talk; that’s a config change and a small infra rollout (approx 1 day of infra ops to create per-tenant namespaces + migration plan).
- No kernel-level changes required; this is at preprocessing layer only.

Risk/rollback plan suggestion:
- Canary at 5% for 48 hours with close telemetry on embedding drift and top-k recall.
- Automated rollback if recall drops >4% for three consecutive hours or error rate increases >1% absolute.

I can produce a short PR with the tokenizer shim by EOD Apr 5 if that helps the timeline.

— Irene
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-05T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary deferment of pin for Vermilion-7B variant (tokenizer mismatch)

Looping in Ops notes and decision: after sync with infra and SRE, we can support a scoped deferment for Zeno Labs under the following conditions:
1) Implement tokenizer shim and per-tenant KV namespace (Irene to deliver PR by EOD Apr 5)
2) Canary at 5% for 48 hours, then ramp to 20% for 24 hours if telemetry is green
3) Telemetry guards: automated rollback triggers as Irene suggested; require real-time dashboard for the Zeno pilot and 2x daily check-ins (first 48 hours)
4) Require Zeno to sign a short intake addendum acknowledging this is a trial and that pinning policy may apply after 14 days if regressions persist

Operational estimate: ~2 engineer-days (Irene + 0.5 day infra ops), SRE on-call for the first 72 hours, and Product to prepare canary criteria doc.

Markus — please schedule the canary window and ensure we have CI artifacts for the alternate tokenizer table. Laura — if Zeno signs the addendum, we can approve the temporary deferment and act as described.

Thanks — moving to comms and scheduling.
Aditya
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
